title: Dev-log build with breakdown and drop
prompt: Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 2,688,000 samples (56.0 s at 30 fps = 1680 frames). Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads, no speech). Fixed random seed (np.random.default_rng(55)). A 56-second 'how it was made' tech bed in F minor at 128 BPM (1 beat = 14.0625 frames). Frames 0-112: muted glitchy intro (bit-crushed 8 kHz, a terminal-cursor tick each beat). Frame 112: full groove: sub kick four-on-the-floor, off-beat sub bass gate (−7 dB pump), Fm9 → Dbmaj7 → Ebsus4 → Cm7 pluck chords, rolling 16th hats; energy flat for 32 bars at -20 dBFS RMS. Frames 1060-1200: gradual brightening, white-noise riser and snare roll accelerating 8ths → 32nds; loudness climbs 4 LU. Frame 1200: 3-beat breakdown to pad only, 20 dB quieter (a near-silence gasp). Frame 1252: re-entry with a downward sub drop (F2→F0 sine sweep 300 ms) and a crash; then 12 bars of the loudest section with bright bell arps (FM, 1/16) and 1/8 chord stabs. Frame 1650: quick fade to 0 by frame 1680. Keep true peak ≤ -1 dBTP even though the drop is loud. Master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled peak check), last frames fade to exactly 0. You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and true peak with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true), check the exact sample count, confirm the energy change lands on each cue frame, check every note fits the chord under it, render a spectrogram PNG and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.

metrics.note: Public out.wav downsampled to 16000 Hz for Workers ≤5 MiB; metrics from 48 kHz master.

notes: 56 s F-minor tech build: muted glitch intro, flat groove, riser/snare roll, near-silence gasp, then louder bell-arp drop.
